paper.citation: Hayden S. Helm, Aranyak Acharyya, Brandon Duderstadt, Youngser Park, Carey E. Priebe, Statistical inference on black-box generative models in the Data Kernel Perspective Space, arXiv:2410.01106.
paper.source_version: Retained paper prose/TeX corresponding to the Helm2025 formalization.

scope: Theorems 1--2, Appendix Assumptions 1--4, Equation (3), and the MDS-consistency dependency used to discharge Equation (3). Experimental claims are excluded.
audit_revision: 2026-08-26 working tree after YWS population-gap/alignment propagation, hypothesis reduction, and Term-2 constant sharpening; based on repository snapshot 8895692fef63 plus the accepted local overlays.

status_definitions.compiled_exact: The source claim is represented by a compiled source-facing theorem with the same mathematical content.
status_definitions.compiled_equivalent: The source claim is compiled under a semantically equivalent encoding; representation changes are documented.
status_definitions.compiled_by_composition: All essential clauses are compiled, but the source result is assembled from multiple declarations rather than one literal wrapper.
status_definitions.compiled_generalized: A compiled theorem is strictly more general or gives a stronger conclusion than the printed source claim.
status_definitions.compiled_specialization: A useful compiled specialization exists, but it does not cover the full printed source scope.
status_definitions.compiled_stronger_hypotheses: The source conclusion is compiled, but the current theorem uses additional or stronger hypotheses.
status_definitions.compiled_source_repair: The source is internally inconsistent or contains a false/overbroad clause; the formalization records the mathematically usable repaired statement.
status_definitions.compiled_role_replaced: The exact source proof lemma is not exposed as a theorem; its role in the main proof is discharged by a different compiled argument. This is not exact source-item coverage.
status_definitions.not_represented: No matching formal theorem or construction was found.
status_definitions.not_proof_debt: The item is exposition, empirical methodology, or an extension beyond the paper theorem surface; it is documented but not counted as missing source theorem coverage.

stronger-analysis-hypotheses.title: The proved risk-transfer wrappers use stronger analytic regularity
stronger-analysis-hypotheses.detail: The paper states sequential/pointwise continuity. Lean retains literal predicates but the main theorems use joint continuity/compact-range sufficient conditions and explicit estimator measurability.

spectral-vs-rawstress-bridge.title: End-to-end spectral bridge needs an eigenvalue floor absent from Helm
spectral-vs-rawstress-bridge.detail: Helm cites the eigengap-free raw-stress consistency theorem from Acharyya 2024. The current end-to-end implementation bridge uses classical spectral MDS and therefore explicitly assumes a population eigenvalue floor (Acharyya 2025 Assumption 2).

diagonal-budget-schedule.title: Theorem 2 is realized along an explicit diagonal budget schedule
diagonal-budget-schedule.detail: The paper writes n,m,r -> infinity. Lean proves existence of a diverging embedding-budget schedule phi(n), a precise diagonalization of the fixed-n convergence used in the proof.

label-compact-support.title: Compact/bounded label support is explicit in Lean but not located in the retained paper source
label-compact-support.detail: Helm2025.DKPS.Theorem1 and Theorem2_bayes require BoundedLabelSupport/LabelCompactSupport so the loss can be uniformly dominated on a compact label range. Searches of the retained prose and TeX did not locate a corresponding paper assumption. This should therefore be treated as an additional formal hypothesis unless a source passage is identified.

dangling-theorem-3-reference.title: The Appendix A.2 proof cites a Theorem 3 that the paper does not contain
dangling-theorem-3-reference.detail: The proof of Theorem 2 concludes "given the results in (Sekhon, 2021), for some subsequence of u as defined in Theorem 3". The retained paper states exactly two theorems -- the TeX source declares thm:rule-convergence and thm:consistency and no third -- so the citation resolves to nothing. The subsequence it appeals to is the one produced inside the Theorem 2 argument itself, which is how the Lean development treats it: Helm2025 proves existence of a diverging embedding-budget schedule rather than importing a numbered result. Recorded so a reviewer asking why the census has no Theorem 3 row gets an answer.

items.title: Fixed-n inference risk transfer
items.source_claim: For fixed n, as DKPS estimation budgets grow, the risk of the decision function trained/evaluated on estimated perspectives converges to the risk based on true perspectives.

semantic_alignment.detail: The conclusion is source-shaped. Lean additionally requires measurable embedding estimators, uses the compact-range form of A3, and joint loss continuity; these are sufficient conditions for the paper proof. The paper-facing wrapper also requires bounded/compact label support; no matching assumption was located in the retained source.

items.notes: The theorem is a genuine paper-facing wrapper, so the remaining mismatch is in hypotheses rather than conclusion. The retained source should be rechecked against the original PDF specifically for label-support/bounded-loss language before treating this hypothesis as source-faithful.

items.title: Consistency transfer from true to estimated DKPS embeddings
items.source_claim: If learning on true perspectives is consistent, learning on estimated perspectives is also consistent as n,m,r grow.

semantic_alignment.detail: Lean proves Bayes-risk consistency along a diverging budget schedule phi(n). The analytic hypotheses are stronger than the literal paper assumptions, and the joint (m,r) limit is represented by diagonalization. The paper-facing wrapper also requires bounded/compact label support; no matching assumption was located in the retained source.

items.notes: The schedule makes the quantifier structure executable rather than leaving the phrase n,m,r -> infinity informal. The retained source should be rechecked against the original PDF specifically for label-support/bounded-loss language before treating this hypothesis as source-faithful.

items.title: Rigid/affine-isometry invariance of the learning rule
items.source_claim: The decision function is unchanged under an orthogonal transformation and translation of the DKPS coordinates.

semantic_alignment.detail: The Lean predicate directly represents invariance under affine isometries of Euclidean embedding space.

items.title: Continuity of the learning rule
items.source_claim: Sequentially close training sets and query points produce close predictions.

semantic_alignment.detail: The literal sequential predicate exists. The main theorem assumes a stronger joint continuity predicate and proves it implies the paper-shaped condition.

items.title: Closed, bounded, complete decision-function image
items.source_claim: Each decision function in the hypothesis class has closed, bounded, complete image.

semantic_alignment.detail: The literal source predicate is retained. The proof uses bounded/compact-range control, equivalent for the finite-dimensional Euclidean codomain used here.

items.title: Continuity of loss in the prediction
items.source_claim: For each fixed label y, the loss varies continuously with the prediction.

semantic_alignment.detail: The literal pointwise-in-label predicate exists, while the main theorem assumes joint continuity of the loss as a convenient sufficient condition.

items.title: Aligned estimated perspectives converge uniformly in probability
items.source_claim: After suitable orthogonal/translation alignment, the maximum coordinate error over the n training models and test model tends to zero in probability.

semantic_alignment.detail: Lean uses a finite iSup in place of max and a single abstract estimation-budget index. For a finite index set this is the same uniform error statement.

items.source_anchor: Appendix A.1 use of Acharyya et al. (2024) alignment consistency
items.title: Discharge Equation (3) from an MDS consistency theorem
items.source_claim: The proof cites the eigengap-free asymptotic raw-stress consistency theorem to obtain aligned DKPS consistency.

semantic_alignment.detail: The available end-to-end bridge realizes the estimator as spectral/classical MDS and therefore assumes a positive population eigenvalue floor. That is stronger than the Helm paper route through raw-stress consistency.

items.notes: This discrepancy belongs to the bridge, not the abstract Theorem1/Theorem2 transfer once Equation (3) is assumed.
items.next_action: For exact end-to-end faithfulness, bridge Helm to the Acharyya2024 raw-stress consistency theorem instead of the spectral estimator, or state the extra spectral assumption in the paper-facing theorem.
